correctness.rationale: For a>0 each supporting sphere contributes the cap on the opposite side of the midplane, and both have area 2πR²(1−a). Sphere area in axial coordinate and azimuth is constant; the seam has measure zero and at a=0 the construction partitions a sphere into hemispheres. Independently integrated the two-point fourth power by averaging over the azimuth difference, treating same-cap and opposite-cap pairs separately. For b=1−a and R=1 this gives μ=2b and ν=4b²(b²−2b+5)/3; scaling restores the stated R factors. The dimensionless ratio (4+a²)/3 is strictly increasing on [0,1), so a and then R are uniquely recovered; the ball is included and a=1 excluded. The bound follows from |a₁²−a₂²|≥|a₁−a₂|², with equality against a=0 setting the constant and exponent. One positive even moment can be held fixed over varying a by scaling R. The independently integrated one-cap case also gives the claimed shared wedge, with distinct surfaces off the full-sphere endpoint. value.rationale: This is a complete inverse law for two natural rigid-motion invariant statistics on a geometrically motivated family. It specifies what can be recovered from two moments, the sharp loss of resolution near a ball, and a concrete ambiguity if the family is unknown. These are not consequences of a general distance expansion alone, and they are exact population statements, not statistical guarantees.
